syllabus.clause: what a table catalog actually does: namespace, current-metadata pointer with compare-and-swap, access control and credential issuance; the legacy options (Hive Metastore, AWS Glue Data Catalog, JDBC catalog) and their limits for multi-engine, multi-cloud estates.

at.step: Reveal: the legacy options, named with their limits
Reveal: why this matters for a multi-cloud estate

items.item: An atomic swap of one table metadata file for another provides the basis for serializable isolation
The atomic swap can be implemented as a pointer in a metastore or database updated with a check-and-put (compare-and-swap) operation
The REST catalog protocol has a real endpoint to load vended credentials for a table from the catalog
Catalog configuration may contain credentials used for subsequent requests for a table
A namespace is defined as a reference to one or more levels

at.step: Reveal: why this matters for a multi-cloud estate

items.item: The catalog's pointer compare-and-swap reuses the exact put-if-absent primitive this chapter has used since topic 13, making the connection explicit rather than inventing a parallel mechanism.
Access control is checked and enforced before the compare-and-swap is attempted, demonstrated by a real PermissionError raised prior to any pointer-file write, not merely a CAS that happens to fail.
The issued credential is a real, scoped data structure naming the exact table's storage prefix and a real TTL, not a placeholder string.
Hive Metastore's limit is stated precisely as a credential-vending gap, not a blanket claim of no access control at all, correcting what a casual reading of the syllabus clause might imply.

items.item: The three named multi-cloud limits (vendor lock-in, no credential vending, single region/account) are each traced to a specific sourced mechanism (whose metastore, which bolted-on service, what scope) rather than listed as abstract complaints.

items.item: The namespace-management demo enforces real uniqueness (a duplicate create is rejected) rather than being a no-op dictionary with no real constraint.
No deltalake/delta-rs/iceberg-python library is used; the catalog is built entirely from this script's own code, matching the chapter's established from-scratch convention.
The scope boundary explicitly names what is not rebuilt (a thrift server, Glue's actual API, AWS STS) rather than silently omitting it.
The predict step at step 2 and the predict step at step 5 are both answered correctly by the reveal steps that immediately follow them.
